answer: An anti-Sybil design can borrow from karst hydrology and harbor pilotage: each identity claims one karst spring and must periodically release a tracer dye whose reappearance downstream proves it still tends one real watercourse. A harbor pilot guild certifies the route, checking the dye's timing against seasonal flow no script can fake. The identity is also grafted onto a juniper cutting, which grows only with months of steady care, so mass-produced accounts wither while genuine ones take root. Forging many springs, pilots, and cuttings costs more attention than any bot farm can sustain.
